what_it_does: In semiconductor manufacturing, chips are patterned using light (photolithography), but after exposure the resist (the light-sensitive material) undergoes a heating step called post-exposure bake. During this bake, chemical reactions spread the light-induced changes throughout the resist layer, and the final chip pattern depends critically on getting these diffusion dynamics right. Simulating this requires modeling 3D diffusion of reactive molecules and their interactions. This paper proposes SDM-PEB, which uses a modern deep learning architecture (Mamba, a recent alternative to traditional attention-based models) to efficiently simulate the physics. The model uses hierarchical feature extraction to capture both coarse patterns and fine details, plus a specialized sparse attention mechanism that exploits the structure of 3D physics to reduce computation.
